# A cross-reference target the level fold rewrites

The LaTeX back-end stores three levels and folds everything deeper into the
third, so a deep entry prints a path the author never spelled. A target naming
that entry has to be folded the same way, or it names a path the printed index
does not contain and a reader following it finds nothing. Judging targets
against what entries PRINT is what makes the two agree; the fold is this
back-end's alone, so HTML and the formats with no back-end keep judging
against what the author wrote.

Depth four, `see=`. The entry: [ash]{.index entry="Ash!Bay!Cod!Dun"}. The
target naming it: [elm]{.index entry="Elm" see="Ash!Bay!Cod!Dun"}.

Depth five, `see-also=`, where the printed third level joins two folded levels
and one of them carries a literal `!` the argument has to quote — a character
makeindex reads inside an encapsulation argument exactly as it reads it inside
an entry key. The entry: [fir]{.index entry="Fir!Gum!Ha!Iv!J!!t"}. The target:
[koa]{.index entry="Koa" see-also="Fir!Gum!Ha!Iv!J!!t"}.

A folded entry carrying a sort key, where the path it FILES under and the path
it PRINTS are different strings. The target must fold to the printed one: a
sort key never appears in the index a reader reads. The entry:
[lime]{.index entry="Lime!Moss!Nut!Orb" sort="zu!ya!xr!wh"}. The target:
[pine]{.index entry="Pine" see="Lime!Moss!Nut!Orb"}.

A target on a contested key — a term marked both plainly and with a
cross-reference — where the surviving target is folded into the entry's own
printed text rather than into an encapsulation. It is a second place a target
is rendered, and a fold applied only at the first would leave it unfolded:
[zinc]{.index entry="Zinc"} and [zed]{.index entry="Zinc"
see="Ash!Bay!Cod!Dun"}.

# What the fold does not change

A target whose folded form still names no printed path is reported, exactly as
one that dangles without any fold: [reed]{.index entry="Reed"
see-also="Sil!Tea!Urn!Vin"}.

A target needing no fold is untouched, and is what tells a rule that folds
what has to be folded from one that rewrites every target:
[wax]{.index entry="Wax" see="Elm"}.

A target naming the contested key, so that the entry a target is compared
against is one whose printed field carries a folded cross-reference of its own:
[yak]{.index entry="Yak" see="Zinc"}.

A target naming a PARENT level of a folded entry resolves, because the set a
target is judged against holds every parent path as well as every whole one.
This is the shape a printed-path set built from whole paths alone would report
as dangling: [yam]{.index entry="Yam" see="Ash!Bay"}.
